title: Remote-harvest postcondition proving the harvest did something
question_or_target: Implement the postcondition for spec failure class 'remote harvest silently does nothing' at line 11319: a harvest run must assert a nonzero delta in harvested artifacts, or terminate as FAILED. Exact target: a harvest that returns exit 0 having transferred nothing must be classified FAILED, not SUCCESS.

implementation.rule: SUCCESS requires process_exit_code==0 AND a nonempty dest delta (new or changed artifact paths). Dest already containing files is not a harvest.
implementation.retry_policy: max 2 attempts; backoff 30s/120s in production CLI default; evidence runs used --backoff-seconds 0

evidence.claim: Deliberately empty harvest: copy step exit 0 transferring 0->0 files and 0->0 bytes was classified FAILED / silent-noop-harvest, not SUCCESS. CLI exit was nonzero. Live emitter re-run: state=FAILED attempts=2.

Nonempty harvest of the planted remote tree: before files=0 bytes=0 after files=3 bytes=350 (delta files=3 bytes=350) classified SUCCESS. Independent walk matched. Emitter re-run after=3 files / 350 bytes.

retry.policy: max 2 attempts, backoff 30s/120s; escalate if the second harvest is also empty. Evidence runs used backoff 0. Retry control: empty remote then fill between attempts reached SUCCESS on attempt 2.

tests.requirement: empty-harvest test must FAIL the run
nonempty-harvest test must pass; a harvester that passes both is not discriminating

negative_controls.description: Classifying exit 0 as SUCCESS with no delta check must PASS an empty harvest; the live classifier must not.
A dest that already contains files plus an empty remote must still be FAILED. A mutant that treats dest stock as SUCCESS fires; live classify does not.
A harvester that passes both empty and nonempty is not discriminating.
negative_controls.bad_state_output: would-be: empty SUCCESS and nonempty SUCCESS
